   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Alan Sharvell, HARROW





Dear Brian and Ron,

Thanks for including my beefs in
OUTLET. Here are another couple
of queries with which your read-
ers may be of some assistance.

Browsing around our local chari-
ty shop I came across LASER
GENIUS by OCEAN for Amstrad and
Spectrum. Unfortunately, the
manual covers tapes but it only
came with a 3" disc. How do you
get it to work? It catalogues OK
but no joy otherwise.


Also, although I have recently
acquired a lot of 3" discs, it
is obvious that 3.5" are cheaper
and hold more info. Richardson
and Co advertise an uncased 3.5"
with leads for the Spectrum at
around `32 (a bit cheaper than
the +D) which equals about 16
discs(3").Would it be compatible
with OUTLET 3.5" or not?

When you start your PC OUTLET
will it be 3.5" FDD or HDD? It
may be of interest for my grand-
son's 386. When it appears he
will be 10 years old then and
more interested in PCs.

        Yours sincerely,

         Alan Sharvell

Brian Cavers to Alan Sharvell

Regarding LASER GENIUS, load
CATDB from last month's OUTLET,
put your LASER GENIUS disc in
the drive and run CATDB. It will
give a more detailed CAT of the
files. Remember, there may be
more than one page of files.

First look for any file called
"DISK". If you see one then
simply reset until you see the
loader menu appear and then
press ENTER to load it.

If there is no file called
"DISK" then write down any with
the letter "P" in the centre of
the screen to the right of their
filename. These are BASIC.


Next, reset, enter +3 BASIC and
load each file you have on your
list using simply LOAD "NAME".
Just reset if you get any error
messages until eventually,if the
thing works at all, you must get
some sort of screen display to
indicate it has loaded.

At some future time you might
prefer to rename the program
that loaded to "DISK" so you can
load it from the +3 menu loader
but I would recommend you always
make a back up of the whole disc
first.

Now study the manual. It should
load and save more or less the
same way as for tape.All you can
do is try it.


I have not seen a recent advert
for Richardson and Co. but if he
has 3.5" drives on offer with
leads for Spectrum I assume he
means as a "B" drive for the +3.
It will certainly save you money
to store files on the larger
format but our 3.5" OUTLET is
for the +D and Disciple and will
not run on that format.


You will need a special routine
to format the discs to their
full capacity of around 800K as
they will only format to the +3
standard 173K with the normal
FORMAT command.If Richardson and
Co. do not supply this routine
with the drive then there is one
in OUTLET 48 called BFORMAT.


Our PC OUTLET will come on a 3.5
high density(HD) disc with about
1.5 megabytes capacity. There is
also a chance it might be avail-
able on a 5.25 HD disc with a
slightly smaller capacity but it
depends on demand.

                           Brian

From Geoff Harris, HALESOWEN

Dear Ron,

I must confess to having prob-
lems with MASTERFILE on my +3 so
at my wits end I write to you.

I cannot merge data files using
MFILE; with MFPLUS3 I can't even
load!...

DISK 75B, MFILE...

C(CAT)
gives.."variable not found 4002"

L(LOAD)  "OUTDEX1.63"
then...
L(MERGE) "+OUTDX64.74"
gives...        "out of memory"


DISK 76B, MFPLUS3


C OK
      ..change to disk 75B


L "OUTDEX1.63"
gives..        "error code 07"


            Yours,

         Geoff Harris


Brian Cavers to Geoff Harris

The CAT D error is my fault - it
is a leftover from converting
from the +D. I also found a bug
in the SAVE/VERIFY routine in
that there is no VERIFY on a +3
disc (which I foresaw) but I put
the test in the wrong place and
the tape save crashes.

I have put a corrected BASIC in
this month's ADDENDERS in the +3
version only. This is the BASIC
only - not the code - so it will
not run in this issue.You should
copy the file to the disc with
the code. If you don't know how
to copy then load it and enter
RUN 9972(with the target disc in
the drive).


You cannot merge OUTDX64.74 into
OUTDEX1.63. My instructions(part
1, page 6) were probably not
clear enough. I did say that
OUTDEX1.63 was full but perhaps
that could be taken to mean the
"whole of the original". Anyway,
it is full and OUTDX64.74 is the
start of the next "volume". If
they could be merged I would
have merged them myself and put
them in as one file in the first
place. What you need to merge is
each new OUTDEX file into
OUTDX64.74, eg, keep adding
OUTDEX.75, OUTDEX.77 etc.

All the above files are MF 48K
files and cannot be loaded into
MF+3 which uses a different type
of file.


If you want to have a go at con-
verting them then look at Chap-
ter 12, p.44 of the MF+3 info.
Use the file CONV which is on
the disc. However, I could not
get it to directly load OUTDEX
files so I loaded one into the
old MF 48K, resaved it as "X"
and then it loaded! Presumably
CONV did not like the filename
of OUTDEX1.63 as it gave "file
not found"!

Once loaded into CONV enter
TICULPAMS as the data refs. You
then need to create a dummy file
in MF+3 with these refs and
use the IMPORT ASCII function to
load the OUTDEX data (see p.59
of part 3 of the MF+3 info).That
is the easy bit!..


I did not go any further than
checking CONV as I could see
that the format would have to be
sorted out and it could be quite
a messy job I reckon.If you save
the result it could probably be
used for future OUTDEX data too.

If you or anyone wants to have a
go then you can send in the
format data but we have no plans
to include OUTDEX in MF+3 format
on a monthly basis!

                         Brian

From Barry Edgeway, NORFOLK

I use SPECFILE+ for a lot of my
various files that I keep on
hobbies and suchlike. I have
adapted the colours to suit
myself as I found the inbuilt
white on blue too much so mine
is now black on white paper
which is much easier to read.
SPECFILE is a very useful util-
ity but one thing I'd like it to
do is to enhance (INVERSE or
FLASH) the keyword (X$) within
the screen array(E$(15,32)).With
some of my files it would be so
useful to be able to highlight
in this way rather than having
to read through a whole file to
find the reference I am looking
for. Can anyone help please?
                     B. Edgeway

Brian Cavers to B. Edgeway

I don't know SPECFILE but it
seems clear from what you say
that it is written in BASIC with
the key elements in BASIC string
variables. If the keyword string
X$ is entered by the user with
the normal BASIC INPUT then you
can simply precede it with the
FLASH or INVERSE codes.There are
two ways of doing this. You can
enter the codes yourself when
entering the keyword thus...

Press the INV VIDEO key just
before typing the keyword to get
the keyword in INVERSE.

Press EXTEND, then SHIFT 9 just
before the keyword to get FLASH.


You can also get BRIGHT by
pressing EXTEND then 9 on its
own or even combine BRIGHT and
FLASH one after the other.

The other way is to alter the
BASIC so that just after the
INPUT X$ (if that is how it is
done) you add to a following
line...


LET X$= CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 1 +X$

       ...for INVERSE or replace
the 20 with 19 for BRIGHT or 18
for FLASH.

Various problems may arise but
there are two common ones that
you must expect...


Whenever X$ is printed with say,
the FLASH code, everything that
is printed after it in the same
PRINT statement will also FLASH
unless you include a FLASH OFF
code. For example, suppose the
keyword in X$ is "MIDBIT"...


PRINT "FIRSTBIT";X$;"LASTBIT"

    ...will display "FIRSTBIT"
normally, then the keyword
"MIDBIT" will be flashing and
then the "LASTBIT" which will
also be flashing!

If the program inserts the above
into the array E$ it will still
flash. If this is the problem
then you need to use...


LET X$= CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 1 + X$ +
CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 0

              ...or, if entering
them directly into the input you
must press EXTEND then SHIFT 8
to switch off FLASH, EXTEND then
8 alone to switch off BRIGHT and
TRUE VIDEO to turn off INVERSE.

The next most likely problem is
that the format display will go
wrong. Each code uses two bytes
(two character spaces).It sounds
like E$(15,32) is 15 lines of 32
characters on each. If a keyword
of 6 characters is included in a
line with two extra FLASH codes
then it will use 8 characters of
the E$ line which will then fall
short of the end of the line by
two characters thus...

Here's an example of a normal
line...

THURSDAY SATURDAY TUESDAY FRIDAY

   ...if the keyword is SATURDAY
and includes two flash codes at
the start then it may show as..

THURSDAY SATURDAY TUESDAY FRID

      ...where SATURDAY will be
flashing (TUESDAY and FRID may
be flashing too!) and FRIDAY is
cut short to FRID. Or, it may
show as...

THURSDAY SATURDAYUESDAY FRIDAY

     ..it all depends how the
routine is programmed.


You need to experiment. It may
be that you can enter a shorter
word for the keyword but then
all the text will display but it
will simply be slightly shorter
on the line...

THURSDAY MONDAY TUESDAY FRIDAY

        ...where the shorter key
word MONDAY is substituted for
SATURDAY. With its two FLASH
codes the total characters on
the line is still 32 so it fits
into the E$ line and no other
characters get missed or over-
written but the line is short at
the end.

All this is guesswork as I have
no idea how the program works!


Another possibility is that the
keyword X$ is simply overprinted
at a certain place in which case
just alter the line that does it
to...

       PRINT FLASH 1;X$

Your best bet is to experiment
with some of the above ideas to
see what results you get and
then write in again.Ideally,send
a listing or even the program.

                          Brian

From Chris Oliver, STAFFS.

Wonder if anyone else who uses
BetaDos or G+Dos has noticed a
strange error report which quite
often appears on my system? The
Error message is the rare...

     "I FOR without NEXT"
                    ...not to be
confused with the more common...

     "1 NEXT without FOR"

But the odd thing is that it
shows the error to be in line
zero which doesn't exist -yet it
is a statement number which
turns out to be correct once one
has tracked down the real reason
for the error stopping the
program...

Every time so far that I have
found the real error in these
circumstances, it has been an
undeclared variable. So the true
report should have been...

   "2 Variable not found"!

The bug has probably been inher-
ited from G+Dos or maybe from
Beijing? Anyway, I'll be very
interested to hear from anyone
suffering from similar symptoms.

                        Chris

Brian Cavers to Chris Oliver

The legitimate"FOR WITHOUT NEXT"
almost never happens as it needs
TWO errors - A missing "NEXT"
and a "FOR n = 1 TO 0" with no
following "STEP -1" so it does
not go throough the loop at all.
This is an alternate way of
forcing a jump to another part
of BASIC and even jumps over a
"STOP" command!!! Try...
   10 FOR G = 1 TO 0
 ...hundreds of lines of program
 6001 STOP
 6002 STOP
 6003 STOP
 6004 NEXT G
 6005 NEXT G
 6006 NEXT G
 6500 BEEP 1,1 : NEXT G : PRINT
     "This is impossible": STOP

Having sent the above reply to
Chris directly he wrote back...

"Paul [Oliver] has just popped
in to see what I'm doing, and
pointed out that if you print
"G" at any stage above, it
appears to be incrementing in a
positive direction! Therefore
one would expect a program...
  10 FOR G= 1 TO 0
  20 PRINT G : NEXT G
  30 STOP
   ...to print 1 to 256ish ?????
In fact it prints nothing, and
leaps straight to the STOP! See
you at the Funny-Farm!"

NEXT patient please!
                      Brian

Brian Cavers to Ronald Raaijen

We put MASTERFILE +3 on the +3
version of OUTLET(Issue 76) only
because it will not run on other
systems and is not easily conv-
ertible. It accesses the drive
by machine code and uses header-
less files for data.I don't know
if there was ever any other 128K
MASTERFILE, perhaps running on
tape, with the LOAD and SAVE
syntax in BASIC.

Your Interface 1 disc system
sounds interesting but our CAT-
LOADER will not work on it. It's
not just a change in BASIC
syntax that is needed; CATLOADER
needs a machine code routine to
read the disc directory.


Clearly your system will be tot-
ally different if it can handle
680K discs! If I had your system
and two months to spare it would
still be difficult!

I recommend you set up simple
menu loaders on each disc as the
boot files and just add the main
program names as needed.At least
you'll be able to load programs
easily...
   10 PRINT "PROG1"
   20 PRINT "PROG2"  etc...

  100 PAUSE 0
  110 IF INKEY$="1" THEN
      LOAD "D";1;"PROG1" etc...

  200 GOTO 100
                           Brian

Brian Cavers to Ron Smith

Let me take first your statement
that"there is no need to reprint
this letter in OUTLETTERS if it
will save time and effort; your
advice and answers.. suffice"

This misunderstanding comes up
frequently so I like to take
every opportunity to air our
position!...

1. We cannot spare the time to
give individuals private advice
by mail except where there is
some fault with a disc or order
etc.The price of OUTLET includes
only the magazine any help that
is in it - there is no hotline
or "help-by-mail" service.Sorry!


2. By publishing readers' prob-
lems and any help we can offer
in OUTLETTERS not only does the
person with the problem get help
but the information is shared
with everyone else.This not only
helps anyone else with the same
or a similar problem but it is
also of interest to many others
simply because we all share the
common interest of the Spectrum.

3. Some readers seeking help may
feel their problem is trivial
with no interest to others. They
may even think the answer will
be obvious to everyone else and
make them look ignorant. Nothing
could be further from the truth;
we are all learning - especially
me!


4. You may get advice from other
readers if I cannot help or in
addition to any help I can give.
Indeed, they may CORRECT any BAD
advice I give!

The advantages of sharing out-
weigh disadvantages.The central
philosophy of OUTLET is an "out-
let for sharing info" etc.

None of the above is to be taken
personally but is intended only
to clarify. Indeed, the wording
of your letter suggests you may
think it could "save my time and
effort" but this is not true. I
only published your letter due
to that proviso; if you had said
categorically "DO NOT PUBLISH" I
would not have:you'd have got no
help at all!

Now to your specific questions..

The +3 defaults to "expanded"
mode - that is, when reset or
first switched on it assumes the
print mode selected by the comm-
and FORMAT LPRINT "E". Sinclair
keyword tokens are stored in
BASIC as single bytes, e.g., the
command PRINT is not stored as
the letters P, R, I, N, T but as
the value 245. Whenever you list
a program on screen,the Spectrum
knows this and every time it
comes to a 245 it "expands" it
into the word PRINT.

When you print on a printer you
may or may not want this to
happen. If you LLIST you DO and
so should select "E" mode.


If, however, you want to send
control codes to your printer
you may need to send the number
245 as it is and so you do NOT
want it expanded into the word
PRINT. You would then use "U"
mode (selected by using the
command FORMAT LPRINT "U").

Therefore, when you first switch
on your +3 and enter...

  10 LLIST
              ...and RUN it your
+3 must send the listing to your
printer unless either the +3 or
the printer cable are faulty. I
doubt it is the +3 as it is hard
to see how it could produce that
type of fault and the fact that
you can COPY SCREEN$ indicates
your cable is OK.

You do not say what results you
get when you try to LLIST.Do you
get totally unreadable garbage
printed or parts of the listing
mixed with rubbish or simply no
response from your printer at
all (or even line feeds but no
text printed)?

Your statements that you cannot
LPRINT or CAT #3 suggests you
are getting nothing at all yet
the fact that you can COPY the
screen makes this seem totally
impossible. If values from the
screen reach the printer then
LPRINT ought to.

I wonder if this is that old +3
bug? This only affects some +3's
but can be fixed thus...


1. Put any recent OUTLET disc
   in drive A.

2. Press the RESET button.

3. Enter +3 BASIC.

4. Enter MERGE "DISK"

5. Wait until OK appears.

6. Enter GO SUB 1002.

7. Enter LLIST.

If it works then delete all the
lines in the program EXCEPT 1002
(by just entering each line num-
ber with no text). Save just the
line 1002 on another disc and
merge it in any suitable program
as needed.

If that doesn't work, study your
printer manual to see if there
are any special switches (apart
from the dip switches) that may
select a special mode in which
normal LPRINT does not work,eg,
some special graphics mode.

I don't know of any change to
HANDYDUMP but try SCOPY in Issue
66 which is virtually the same.
Ah! You say AREA FIND prints OK.
This is not the same as HANDY
DUMP but simply LPRINTS. The
light blue printer prompt bar at
the bottom of OUTLET screens is
pretty much the same whether the
actual routine is a graphics
dump or just LPRINTing - it is
simply to select the hardware
syntax.


This supports the theory that it
is the old +3 bug. Each time you
load OUTLET the bug is fixed.Try
resetting, enter +3 BASIC and
load AREA.071 by direct command.
It probably will not work now.If
so, extract line 1002 from our
DISK loader as described and
that should solve your problems;
otherwise write in with more
details of the exact results you
get when trying to LPRINT.


By the way, line 1002 may not be
a convenient number for many of
your programs but you cannot
change its number by editing it
directly as it will corrupt. Use
the renumber option on the +3
edit menu instead.


My +3 does not suffer from the
printer bug and so I have not
explored it nor know much about
it. However, there are a couple
of POKEs which essentially do
the same job as our line 1002
and these may be more convenient
for general use. Our line 1002
was contributed by someone more
expert on the +3 than me and I
think it does slightly more than
the POKEs. However,I cannot find
a note of the POKEs although I'm
sure they have been in OUTLET
before. Can anyone else send
these in again please?

Regarding your B drive, remember
BFORMAT in OUTLET 48 which also
gives a 700K + format on a 3.5"
double-density drive.     Brian

Well enough of me on my soapbox;
why I write this is for a few

Can anyone help please? B. Edgeway

Brian Cavers to B. Edgeway

I don't know SPECFILE but it seems clear from what you say that it is written in BASIC with the key elements in BASIC string variables. If the keyword string X$ is entered by the user with the normal BASIC INPUT then you can simply precede it with the FLASH or INVERSE codes.There are two ways of doing this. You can enter the codes yourself when entering the keyword thus...

Press the INV VIDEO key just before typing the keyword to get the keyword in INVERSE.

Press EXTEND, then SHIFT 9 just before the keyword to get FLASH.

You can also get BRIGHT by pressing EXTEND then 9 on its own or even combine BRIGHT and FLASH one after the other.

The other way is to alter the BASIC so that just after the INPUT X$ (if that is how it is done) you add to a following line...

LET X$= CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 1 +X$

...for INVERSE or replace the 20 with 19 for BRIGHT or 18 for FLASH.

Various problems may arise but there are two common ones that you must expect...

Whenever X$ is printed with say, the FLASH code, everything that is printed after it in the same PRINT statement will also FLASH unless you include a FLASH OFF code. For example, suppose the keyword in X$ is "MIDBIT"...

PRINT "FIRSTBIT";X$;"LASTBIT"

...will display "FIRSTBIT" normally, then the keyword "MIDBIT" will be flashing and then the "LASTBIT" which will also be flashing!

If the program inserts the above into the array E$ it will still flash. If this is the problem then you need to use...

LET X$= CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 1 + X$ + CHR$ 20 + CHR$ 0

...or, if entering them directly into the input you must press EXTEND then SHIFT 8 to switch off FLASH, EXTEND then 8 alone to switch off BRIGHT and TRUE VIDEO to turn off INVERSE.

The next most likely problem is that the format display will go wrong. Each code uses two bytes (two character spaces).It sounds like E$(15,32) is 15 lines of 32 characters on each. If a keyword of 6 characters is included in a line with two extra FLASH codes then it will use 8 characters of the E$ line which will then fall short of the end of the line by two characters thus...

Here's an example of a normal line...

THURSDAY SATURDAY TUESDAY FRIDAY

...if the keyword is SATURDAY and includes two flash codes at the start then it may show as..

THURSDAY SATURDAY TUESDAY FRID

...where SATURDAY will be flashing (TUESDAY and FRID may be flashing too!) and FRIDAY is cut short to FRID. Or, it may show as...

THURSDAY SATURDAYUESDAY FRIDAY

..it all depends how the routine is programmed.

You need to experiment. It may be that you can enter a shorter word for the keyword but then all the text will display but it will simply be slightly shorter on the line...

THURSDAY MONDAY TUESDAY FRIDAY

...where the shorter key word MONDAY is substituted for SATURDAY. With its two FLASH codes the total characters on the line is still 32 so it fits into the E$ line and no other characters get missed or over- written but the line is short at the end.

All this is guesswork as I have no idea how the program works!

Another possibility is that the keyword X$ is simply overprinted at a certain place in which case just alter the line that does it to...

PRINT FLASH 1;X$

Your best bet is to experiment with some of the above ideas to see what results you get and then write in again.Ideally,send a listing or even the program.

Brian Cavers to Ron Smith

Let me take first your statement that"there is no need to reprint this letter in OUTLETTERS if it will save time and effort; your advice and answers.. suffice"

This misunderstanding comes up frequently so I like to take every opportunity to air our position!...

1. We cannot spare the time to give individuals private advice by mail except where there is some fault with a disc or order etc.The price of OUTLET includes only the magazine any help that is in it - there is no hotline or "help-by-mail" service.Sorry!

2. By publishing readers' prob- lems and any help we can offer in OUTLETTERS not only does the person with the problem get help but the information is shared with everyone else.This not only helps anyone else with the same or a similar problem but it is also of interest to many others simply because we all share the common interest of the Spectrum.

4. You may get advice from other readers if I cannot help or in addition to any help I can give. Indeed, they may CORRECT any BAD advice I give!

I only published your letter due to that proviso; if you had said categorically "DO NOT PUBLISH" I would not have:you'd have got no help at all!

Now to your specific questions..

The +3 defaults to "expanded" mode - that is, when reset or first switched on it assumes the print mode selected by the comm- and FORMAT LPRINT "E". Sinclair keyword tokens are stored in BASIC as single bytes, e.g., the command PRINT is not stored as the letters P, R, I, N, T but as the value 245. Whenever you list a program on screen,the Spectrum knows this and every time it comes to a 245 it "expands" it into the word PRINT.

When you print on a printer you may or may not want this to happen. If you LLIST you DO and so should select "E" mode.

If, however, you want to send control codes to your printer you may need to send the number 245 as it is and so you do NOT want it expanded into the word PRINT. You would then use "U" mode (selected by using the command FORMAT LPRINT "U").

Therefore, when you first switch on your +3 and enter...

10 LLIST ...and RUN it your +3 must send the listing to your printer unless either the +3 or the printer cable are faulty. I doubt it is the +3 as it is hard to see how it could produce that type of fault and the fact that you can COPY SCREEN$ indicates your cable is OK.

You do not say what results you get when you try to LLIST.Do you get totally unreadable garbage printed or parts of the listing mixed with rubbish or simply no response from your printer at all (or even line feeds but no text printed)?

Your statements that you cannot LPRINT or CAT #3 suggests you are getting nothing at all yet the fact that you can COPY the screen makes this seem totally impossible. If values from the screen reach the printer then LPRINT ought to.

I wonder if this is that old +3 bug? This only affects some +3's but can be fixed thus...

1. Put any recent OUTLET disc in drive A.

2. Press the RESET button.

3. Enter +3 BASIC.

4. Enter MERGE "DISK"

5. Wait until OK appears.

6. Enter GO SUB 1002.

По умолчанию +3 находится в режиме «expanded» — то есть при сбросе или первом включении он предполагает режим печати, выбранный командой FORMAT LPRINT "E". Токены ключевых слов Sinclair хранятся в BASIC в виде отдельных байтов, например, команда PRINT хранится не в виде букв P, R, I, N, T, а как число 245. Всякий раз, когда вы выводите листинг программы на экран, Spectrum знает об этом и каждый раз, когда натыкается на 245, «разворачивает» его в слово PRINT.

При выводе на принтер вам может требоваться или не требоваться это разворачивание. Если вы делаете LLIST, оно вам ТРЕБУЕТСЯ, и поэтому следует выбрать режим «E».

Если же вы хотите отправить управляющие коды на принтер, вам может понадобиться отправить число 245 как есть, и поэтому вы НЕ хотите, чтобы оно разворачивалось в слово PRINT. В таком случае вы бы использовали режим «U» (выбирается командой FORMAT LPRINT "U").

Поэтому, когда вы впервые включаете свой +3 и вводите...

```text
  10 LLIST
```
...и запускаете его (RUN), ваш +3 обязан отправить листинг на принтер, если только не неисправен сам +3 или кабель принтера. Я сомневаюсь, что дело в +3, так как трудно представить, как он мог бы выдать подобную неисправность, а тот факт, что вы можете делать COPY SCREEN$, указывает на исправность кабеля.

Вы не говорите, какие результаты получаете при попытке сделать LLIST. Печатается ли совершенно нечитаемый мусор, или куски листинга вперемешку с абракадаброй, или принтер вообще никак не реагирует (или даже переводит строки, но текст не печатает)?

Ваши утверждения о том, что вы не можете сделать LPRINT или CAT #3, наводят на мысль, что вы вообще ничего не получаете на выходе, однако тот факт, что вы можете делать COPY экрана, делает это совершенно невероятным. Если данные с экрана доходят до принтера, то и LPRINT должен работать.

Интересно, не тот ли это старый баг +3? Он затрагивает только некоторые +3, но его можно исправить следующим образом...

1. Вставьте любой свежий диск OUTLET в дисковод A.
2. Нажмите кнопку RESET.
3. Войдите в +3 BASIC.
4. Введите MERGE "DISK"
5. Подождите, пока появится OK.
6. Введите GO SUB 1002.
7. Введите LLIST.

Если это сработает, удалите все строки в программе, КРОМЕ 1002 (просто вводя каждый номер строки без текста). Сохраните одну только строку 1002 на другой диск и объединяйте её (MERGE) с любой нужной программой по мере необходимости.

Если это не поможет, изучите руководство к своему принтеру, чтобы узнать, нет ли там каких-либо специальных переключателей (помимо dip-переключателей), которые могут выбирать специальный режим, в котором обычный LPRINT не работает — например, какой-нибудь специальный графический режим.

Я не знаю ни о каких изменениях в HANDYDUMP, но попробуйте SCOPY в выпуске 66, это практически то же самое. А! Вы говорите, что AREA FIND печатает нормально. Но это не то же самое, что HANDY DUMP, там просто используется LPRINT. Голубая строка подсказки принтера внизу экранов OUTLET выглядит примерно одинаково, независимо от того, является ли сама процедура дампом графики или просто LPRINT'ом — она служит лишь для выбора синтаксиса оборудования.

Это подтверждает теорию о том, что это старый баг +3. Каждый раз при загрузке OUTLET ошибка исправляется. Попробуйте сбросить компьютер, войти в +3 BASIC и загрузить AREA.071 прямой командой. ASCIIGRAMS — это интеллектуальная игра, в которую может играть один или любое количество игроков, на время или без. Это нечто среднее между... ладно, позвольте рассказать, как она появилась...

Как вы знаете, я помогаю Ron и Brian, подготавливая довольно много материалов, присылаемых для OUTLET, и иногда нам попадаются слова, которые оскорбляют интеллект вас, читателей. Поэтому неподобающее слово или фразу приходится менять или убирать. В Бейсике это не проблема, но в машинном коде все гораздо сложнее, особенно если код сжат и по разным причинам его не так-то просто распаковать и сжать заново!!

Вот тут-то и появляется игра. Слово нельзя просто удалить, так как это нарушит декомпрессию, и по тем же причинам его нельзя просто затереть пробелами или заменить на звездочки.

Есть и еще одна сложность: на случай, если в программе есть встроенная зависимость или проверка контрольной суммы байтов, ASCII-коды заменяющих букв в сумме должны давать ровно столько же, сколько давали заменяемые! Итак, правила ASCIIGRAMS:

1). Выберите слово.  
2). Замените его другим существующим словом точно такой же длины, ПРИ ЭТОМ сумма кодов ASCII новых символов должна совпадать с суммой исходных.

Анаграмма, конечно, была бы самым простым решением, но помните, что пробелы считаются за 32.

Вот пример:

Задумаем слово... хм, «BASIC»;  
ASCII-значения:

```text
  B  A  S  I  C
  66 65 83 73 67  = сумма 354
```

Его можно заменить на:

```text
  F  A  C  E  S
  70 65 67 69 83  = сумма 354
```

Уф! Выглядит просто, но попробуйте сами!  
Веселитесь.
